asr_spotcheck.notes: First-minute ASR follows the intended opening and shows no spoken speaker labels. ASC is transcribed as A-C, which is the source acronym context and not an ALIUS spelling issue.
asr_spotcheck.excerpt:
For many anthropologists today, the Western category altered states of consciousness
A-C is still haunted by the ghost of pathologization.
Some of them have instead proposed the use of culture, specific concepts such as symptomatic
consciousness, or autonomous imagination or shamanic state of consciousness.
They believe these terms will be more in sync with experiential ground of possession,
but at the same time are more difficult to export as a general analytical category.
In these two attitudes, where would you drag your own epistemological concept?
The problem with the term or category A-C is that it assumes a normative state that is widely
shared and from which certain states can be marked as alterations.
The unmarked normative state that is implied as a self-conscious, reflexive form of awareness
that is highly valued in Euro-American cultures.
Of course, this state may not be the default state for all individuals in all places
at all.
